rationale_evidence.anchor: The structural contest — ownership cannot settle it
rationale_evidence.statement: Both structural candidates (Reference-Architecture and Meta-Model) are owned by the Decision Authority, so the Reference-Architecture-vs-Meta-Model question is not an ownership dispute but a scope/identity question (does 'what the platform IS' mean its components or its element types?). Ownership, the strongest DDD signal available, is silent here, confirming that D-8 must investigate and that labels decide nothing.

rationale_evidence.anchor: CHECK-BEFORE-DISCOVERING — and it reshapes the commission twice
rationale_evidence.statement: Of a prior review's four 'remaining discoveries', three are already done: platform invariants (the 11-invariant set, 10 surviving cross-product projection), lifecycle owners (the Engineering Progression Model P-1..P-10, each with owner), and the Engineering Kernel (A-5, tested and falsified for sufficiency at n=1, MVK). Recording this prevents their re-commissioning. Only the meta-model question is open; and meta-models already exist in the corpus (three formal ones plus two working classifications), so the real question is whether independent passes converge, not whether a meta-model exists.

rationale_evidence.anchor: VERDICT: SUPPORTED — a meta-model HAS emerged. But not the one hypothesized. It is DIMENSIONAL-WITH-ARCHETYPES, not a flat category list
rationale_evidence.statement: Five independent classification passes (RQ-002 Knowledge Meta-Model; Engineering Platform Knowledge Metamodel; L-A knowledge-types.yaml; Relationship Ontology section 2; Progression Model), produced months apart by different exercises, converge on a dimensional-with-archetypes structure rather than a flat category list, refuting the hypothesized A-G flat list — the same error RQ-002 already refuted ('one thing cannot change type by being encoded differently').

rationale_evidence.anchor: Boundary Analysis — The KINDS themselves | KnowledgeOS — the meta-model is platform knowledge; a hospital adopter inherits the kinds and none of the instances
rationale_evidence.statement: The kinds themselves belong to KnowledgeOS (the meta-model is platform knowledge; a different adopter inherits the kinds, not the instances); instances distribute by AUTHORITY-SCOPE, which is why scope must remain a dimension; Runtime Assets are already bounded by R-42 (platform assets only); outside the platform lies external obligations (the CONSTRAINS gap, CV-3/G-3) which the meta-model inherits but does not fill.

rationale_evidence.anchor: Classification — every gap from the projection ... G-1..G-5
rationale_evidence.statement: Five gaps classified by category (Structural/Behavioral/Evolutionary) and cause: G-1 (I-4/ATTESTS/PROJECTION inert-vs-attested) is EVOLUTIONARY, caused by a missing lifecycle, belongs to LIFECYCLE. G-2 (SPECIALIZES, Engineering Knowledge -> product knowledge) is EVOLUTIONARY, a missing relationship, belongs to ONTOLOGY. G-3 (external authority/CONSTRAINS) is BEHAVIORAL, a missing relationship (obligation != ownership), belongs to GOVERNANCE. G-4 (PRODUCT vs DEPLOYMENT/INSTANTIATES) is STRUCTURAL but dissolves: a deployment is a nested Knowledge Space, so it belongs to ONTOLOGY as resolved, no new concept. G-5 (Runtime Adapter disappeared in both new domains) is STRUCTURAL but is a confirmation of Hexagonal behaving correctly, not a failure.
